appraisal_events.evidence: Ces questions froissèrent sans doute Jupien... M. de Charlus... adressa à Jupien une prière... qui toucha assez le giletier pour effacer sa souffrance... de l'air noyé de bonheur de quelqu'un dont on vient de flatter profondément l'amour-propre... Jupien... dit au baron d'un air souriant, ému, supérieur et reconnaissant : « Oui, va, grand gosse ! »
appraisal_events.explanation: After his questions wound Jupien's pride, Charlus must flatter and plead with him to smooth things over; Jupien ends up visibly gratified and answers in a patronizing, superior tone, reversing the expected deference between the aristocratic baron and the tradesman.

appraisal_events.evidence: Dès le début de cette scène, une révolution... s'était opérée en M. de Charlus... c'en était une [femme] ! ... Race sur qui pèse une malédiction et qui doit vivre dans le mensonge et le parjure... exclus même... de la sympathie... de leurs semblables.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's revelation recasts Charlus as belonging to a stigmatized, secretive 'race,' framed through language of curse, deceit, and social exclusion, even as the surrounding reflection also grants this condition dignity and sympathy.

status_effects.explanation: Jupien locally gains the upper hand: Charlus must court and flatter him, and Jupien responds with an indulgent, superior tone rather than deference.
Charlus is shown needing to placate and plead with Jupien to regain his goodwill, a notable reversal of the class deference one would expect from a tradesman toward a baron.

The narrator's extended reflection recasts Charlus within a stigmatized, 'cursed' category, locally lowering him even though the passage's stance toward that category is complex and partly sympathetic.

ambiguities: The narrator's essay on 'la race' of inverts mixes stigmatizing language (curse, lies, exclusion) with sympathy and comparisons to persecuted groups, so how far E2 should be read as endorsed condemnation versus compassionate, ambivalent analysis is genuinely unsettled by the text.
